from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Convolution is a sliding window operator.",
            "Imagine a 3x3 filter passing over pixels.",
            "Multiply pixel values by filter weights.",
            "Sum results to produce new pixel value.",
            "This process smooths digital images."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid visual components
        grid_pixels = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7, stroke_width=2, color=WHITE) for _ in range(25)])
        grid_pixels.arrange_in_grid(rows=5, cols=5, buff=0)
        
        monitor = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/monitor.svg")
        camera = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg")
        
        grid_visual_group = VGroup(grid_pixels, monitor)
        self.place_in_area(grid_visual_group, 'B2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.85)

        # 3x3 window
        window = Square(side_length=2.1, stroke_width=6, color="#FF0000")
        sliding_window_group = VGroup(window)
        self.place_in_area(sliding_window_group, 'C3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_visual_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(window))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(window, color="#FF0000", scale_factor=1.05))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(sliding_window_group.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.7), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#F333FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.place_at_grid(camera, 'D6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Flash(sliding_window_group.get_center(), color="#FFFFFF", line_length=0.2), FadeIn(camera))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", ["Step one: Choose a kernel.", "Step two: Slide, multiply, and sum.", "Step three: Analyze the resulting map."])
        
        # Load SVG Assets
        input_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg", color="#FFFFFF")

        kernel_label = Text("Kernel", color="#FF0000")

        self.place_at_grid(kernel_asset, "C4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(kernel_label, "C5", scale_factor=0.7) # B011
        kernel_label.next_to(kernel_asset, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(feature_map_label, "E4", scale_factor=0.7) # B034
        
        # Arrows (B035)
        arrow_in_to_ker = Arrow(start=input_asset.get_bottom(), end=kernel_asset.get_top(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1)

        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept
sections.content: Define convolution as a sliding window operator. Before introducing the math, visualize a small 'filter' (kernel) passing over a 2D grid of values (pixels). Explain that at each position, we perform an element-wise multiplication and summation.
sections.example: Imagine a 3x3 'blurring lens' hovering over a digital photo of a cat, averaging the pixels beneath it to smooth out noise.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics (Graphical Representation)
sections.content: Transition to the formal discrete formula: (f * g)[n] = Σ f[k]g[n-k]. Use a visual animation where the kernel is 'flipped' and slid across the signal. Highlight the importance of the kernel's values (weights) in determining the output transformation.
sections.example: Represent a 1D sequence [1, 2, 3] being convolved with a filter [0.5, 0.5] to create a simple moving average graph.

sections.title: Application: Feature Detection in Computer Vision
sections.content: Explain how different kernels act as 'detectors.' A kernel with positive values on one side and negative on the other will produce high outputs where brightness changes abruptly—effectively identifying edges.
sections.example: An animation showing a Sobel filter detecting the outline of a robot's chassis by highlighting high-contrast gradients.

sections.title: Real-World Integration: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
sections.content: Synthesize the knowledge. Explain that in modern AI, the computer 'learns' the optimal filter weights to identify complex objects. This is the foundation of image recognition in autonomous vehicles.
sections.example: A diagram showing a smart vacuum cleaner 'seeing' a dog vs. a slipper by passing a series of learned convolution layers over the sensor data.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the three core steps: 1. Choose a kernel, 2. Slide/Multiply/Sum, 3. Analyze the output. Emphasize that convolution is the mathematical 'language' of spatial pattern recognition.
sections.example: A quick visual 'speed-run' showing the transformation of raw pixels into a simplified 'Edge Map' and then into a high-level label: 'Object Detected: Shiba Inu'.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The sliding window animation at 0:02-0:05 overlaps with the lecture text, reducing readability and causing visual clutter. Fix: self.place_in_area(sliding_window_group, 'C3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=2, object=sliding_window_group)
issues.resolution_note: Used place_in_area for sliding_window_group to prevent lecture overlap.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The 'Grid Visual' header and the 6x6 grid in the second scene are poorly balanced, leaving significant dead space while the left side is crowded with text. Fix: self.place_in_area(grid_visual_group, 'B2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.85) (line=7, object=grid_visual_group)
issues.resolution_note: Applied place_in_area for grid_visual_group to optimize balance.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Text block in the second scene is vertically misaligned with the visual grid, creating an unbalanced layout. Fix: self.place_at_grid(lecture_text_block, 'B1', scale_factor=1.0) (line=7, object=lecture_text_block)
issues.resolution_note: Resolved vertical alignment. Note: Used setup_layout default position for text as it's structurally fixed, but ensured grid is adjusted relative to it.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Elements are clustered too close to the top-left, risking interference with lecture text reading flow. Fix: Line 65: self.place_in_area(input_mobj, 'B3', 'B5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=65, object=input_mobj)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed input_mobj positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The kernel is vertically cramped against the input, creating a cluttered visual stack. Fix: Line 66: self.place_in_area(kernel_mobj, 'C3', 'C5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=66, object=kernel_mobj)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed kernel_mobj positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The output cells are placed too low, nearing the edge of the screen and isolating them from the calculation sequence. issues.resolution_note: Fixed output cells positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The kernel matrix is positioned too close to the image area, risking overlap during animation sequences. Fix: Line 64: self.place_at_grid(kernel, 'D5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=64, object=kernel)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The edge detection visualization is currently at E4, which is poorly balanced and too low for the primary visual flow. Fix: Line 73: self.place_at_grid(edge_detection, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7) (line=73, object=edge_detection)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The cnn_stack occupies too much horizontal space (A2-C4), causing it to crowd the center-right area and risk visual clutter. Fix: Line 61: self.place_in_area(cnn_stack, 'A3', 'C5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=61, object=cnn_stack)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The label 'Dog' at E3 is too close to the preceding animation elements, violating the proximity and clarity requirements. Fix: Line 77: self.place_at_grid(label, 'E4', scale_factor=0.9) (line=77, object=label)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Labels 'Window' and 'Kernel' are horizontally aligned with the left-side text, causing potential visual clutter and competing for eye-path. issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The 'Feature Map' label is too low and distant from the kernel, creating poor proximity and awkward white space usage. Fix: Line 58: self.place_at_grid('feature_map', 'C4', scale_factor=0.85) (line=58, object=feature_map)
